# Overview

This practical introduces polygenic risk scores using chromosome 22 GWAS
summary statistics, a European 1000 Genomes LD reference, simulated target
genotypes, and a quantitative outcome.

We will:

1. Use PLINK 1.9 to select approximately independent variants by LD clumping.
2. Use PLINK 2 to calculate a PRS at nine GWAS p-value thresholds.
3. Select a threshold using 10,000 tuning samples.
4. Compare four LDpred2 candidates using prepared results by default, and select one in the tuning set.
5. Compare the two selected scores in 10,000 separate validation samples.

Suggested 90-minute schedule: setup (10 minutes), C+T (30), tuning discussion
(10), LDpred2 (20), comparison (15), and buffer (5). Instructors should install
packages, precompute the LD matrix, and run this document before class.
Students start with **prepared LDpred2 results**. Optional live fitting uses
the supplied LD matrix; switch `ldpred_mode` to `"fit"` to try it. Complete the
session launch, required package checks, and shared-data access check before
the lab. Download the LD matrix beforehand only if you plan to fit live. During class, run chunks in order **or** Knit; doing both repeats the
analysis. The preparation helpers are supplied code, not exercises to rewrite.

For individual \(i\), the score is
\[
\mathrm{PRS}_i = \sum_{j \in S} \widehat\beta_j G_{ij},
\]
where \(S\) is the selected variant set, \(\widehat\beta_j\) is the GWAS
coefficient, and \(G_{ij}\) counts copies of the **effect allele A1**.
This example predicts a quantitative trait, so performance is measured with
linear-regression \(R^2\).

# Prepare RStudio on Biowulf

Start **RStudio Server through Biowulf OnDemand** on a compute node. Start with
**2 CPUs, 8 GB RAM, at least 2 hours, and 5 GB local scratch** for this chromosome
22 exercise. Select **R 4.6** to match the tested environment. The code defaults to one PLINK
thread and a 2,048 MB PLINK workspace. Keep these settings within your allocation.

## Get your own copy

In the RStudio **Terminal** tab, clone the workshop into a directory you own:

```bash

cd "/data/$USER/Stats_Gen/workshop6"
git clone https://github.com/DCEG-workshops/statgen_workshop_tutorial.git
cd statgen_workshop_tutorial/src/06_PRS
pwd
```

If you already have a clone, update it to include `src/06_PRS/` and use that

Every listed file should report `OK`. Run this check before editing the Rmd;
after your own edits, its checksum will differ. On macOS, use

Default prepared mode needs `data.table`, `knitr`, `rmarkdown`, and `Matrix`.
The tested Biowulf R 4.6 module provides these core packages. The installation
block below is for **optional live fitting**; skip it for prepared mode when
the four core packages are already available.

to `src/06_PRS/`. Both `bigsnpr` and `bigsparser` need to be installed for live

```r
dir.create("06_PRS_R_library", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

sample split, and performance tables are saved there.

```{r paths-and-resources}
library(data.table)
setDTthreads(1)
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("SLURM_JOB_ID"))) {
  stop("Run this tutorial inside a Biowulf compute allocation.")
}
threads <- as.integer(params$threads)
allocated_cpus <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK", "1"))
if (is.na(threads) || threads < 1L || threads > allocated_cpus) {
  stop("threads must be between 1 and SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK (or 1 if unset).")
}
memory_mb <- as.integer(params$memory_mb)
if (is.na(memory_mb) || memory_mb < 640L) stop("memory_mb must be at least 640.")
if (!is.finite(params$clump_r2) || params$clump_r2 <= 0 || params$clump_r2 >= 1 ||
    !is.finite(params$clump_kb) || params$clump_kb <= 0) {
  stop("Use 0 < clump_r2 < 1 and clump_kb > 0.")
}
Sys.setenv(OMP_NUM_THREADS = "1", OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS = "1", MKL_NUM_THREADS = "1")

data_dir <- normalizePath(params$data_dir, mustWork = TRUE)
sum_data_file <- file.path(data_dir, "EUR_sum_data")
ref_data <- file.path(data_dir, "1kg_eur_22", "chr_22")
geno_file <- file.path(data_dir, "prs_genotype", "chr22_test")
outcome_file <- file.path(data_dir, "y_out")
inputs <- c(sum_data_file, paste0(ref_data, c(".bed", ".bim", ".fam")),
            paste0(geno_file, c(".bed", ".bim", ".fam")), outcome_file)
missing_inputs <- inputs[!file.exists(inputs) | file.access(inputs, 4) != 0]
if (length(missing_inputs)) stop("Missing/unreadable input: ",
                                 paste(missing_inputs, collapse = ", "))

output_dir <- normalizePath(path.expand(params$output_dir), mustWork = FALSE)
if (output_dir == data_dir || startsWith(output_dir, paste0(data_dir, "/"))) {
  stop("Choose an output_dir outside the shared input directory.")
}
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
run_dir <- tempfile(pattern = paste0("run_", format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"), "_"),
                    tmpdir = output_dir)
if (!dir.create(run_dir)) stop("Cannot create a results directory: ", run_dir)
run_dir <- normalizePath(run_dir)
saveRDS(params, file.path(run_dir, "parameters.rds"))
writeLines(c(paste("Host:", Sys.info()[["nodename"]]),
             paste("Job:", Sys.getenv("SLURM_JOB_ID")),
             paste("Working directory:", getwd()),
             paste("Started:", Sys.time())), file.path(run_dir, "run_info.txt"))
knitr::kable(data.frame(input = sub(paste0(data_dir, "/"), "", inputs, fixed = TRUE),
                        MB = round(file.info(inputs)$size / 1024^2, 2)))
cat("Results directory:", run_dir, "\n")
```

## Run PLINK from R

This helper loads the appropriate Biowulf module in a child shell, records the
command and its output, and stops if PLINK fails. Switching PLINK versions
does not change the RStudio environment.

```{r plink-helper}
run_plink <- function(version, args, label) {
  module_name <- switch(version, "1" = "plink/1.9.0-beta4.4", "2" = "plink/7.1-alpha")
  binary <- switch(version, "1" = "plink", "2" = "plink2")
  if (is.null(module_name)) stop("Unknown PLINK version.")
  command <- paste(c(binary, shQuote(as.character(args))), collapse = " ")
  script <- file.path(run_dir, paste0(label, ".sh"))
  log <- file.path(run_dir, paste0(label, ".console.log"))
  writeLines(c("#!/bin/bash", "set -eo pipefail",
               "if ! type module >/dev/null 2>&1; then source /etc/profile.d/modules.sh; fi",
               paste("module load", shQuote(module_name)), command), script)
  status <- system2("bash", shQuote(script), stdout = log, stderr = log)
  if (status != 0L) stop("PLINK failed; inspect ", log)
  invisible(log)
}
version_logs <- c(run_plink("1", "--version", "plink1_version"),
                  run_plink("2", "--version", "plink2_version"))
cat(unlist(lapply(version_logs, readLines)), sep = "\n")
resource_args <- c("--threads", threads, "--memory", memory_mb)
```

# Inspect the summary statistics and outcomes

`BETA` is the effect per copy of `A1`; it is not an odds ratio. The supplied
files are prepared with consistent variant identifiers and allele coding.
For another dataset, verify genome build, strand, both alleles, and independence
of discovery and target samples before scoring. Matching an rsID alone is
insufficient to establish allele alignment.

```{r read-data}
EUR_sum <- fread(sum_data_file, colClasses = c(SNP = "character", A1 = "character"))
required_columns <- c("CHR", "SNP", "BP", "A1", "TEST", "NMISS", "BETA", "STAT", "P")
if (!all(required_columns %in% names(EUR_sum))) stop("Summary-statistic columns are missing.")
if (anyDuplicated(EUR_sum$SNP)) stop("Duplicate summary SNP IDs.")

fam <- fread(paste0(geno_file, ".fam"), header = FALSE, colClasses = "character")
setnames(fam, c("FID", "IID", "father", "mother", "sex", "phenotype"))
y_out <- fread(outcome_file, colClasses = c(ID = "character"))
if (!all(c("ID", "y") %in% names(y_out))) stop("y_out must contain ID and y.")
if (nrow(y_out) != 20000L || nrow(fam) != 20000L ||
    anyNA(y_out$ID) || anyNA(fam$IID) || anyDuplicated(y_out$ID) ||
    anyDuplicated(fam$IID) || !setequal(y_out$ID, fam$IID) ||
    any(!is.finite(y_out$y))) {
  stop("Expected 20,000 finite outcomes and uniquely matching target IIDs.")
}
# Preserve phenotype order for the split; attach genotype identifiers explicitly.
samples <- data.table(FID = fam$FID[match(y_out$ID, fam$IID)],
                      IID = y_out$ID, y = y_out$y,
                      cohort = rep(c("tuning", "validation"), each = 10000L))
fwrite(samples[, .(FID, IID, cohort)], file.path(run_dir, "sample_split.tsv"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(data.frame(summary_variants = nrow(EUR_sum), target_samples = nrow(samples),
                        tuning_samples = sum(samples$cohort == "tuning"),
                        validation_samples = sum(samples$cohort == "validation")))
```

The first 10,000 rows of `y_out` form the tuning set and the last 10,000 form
the validation set. In the supplied data these are IDs 100001 to 110000 and
110001 to 120000, respectively.
Do not use validation outcomes to choose either method's parameters.


# Prepare one eligible variant pool for both methods

LDpred2 needs both alleles, standard errors, and GWAS sample sizes in addition
to effect estimates. The supplied PLINK `ADD` results report the signed test
statistic, so we reconstruct \(\mathrm{SE}=\mathrm{BETA}/\mathrm{STAT}\).
Rows with undefined or nonpositive SE are excluded. `NMISS` supplies the
per-variant discovery sample size for this quantitative trait, not the target
or reference sample size. Rounded input statistics make the reconstructed SE
approximate; use the original SE column when available in a new study.

These particular SNP IDs encode position and both alleles, for example
`rs62224609:16051249:T:C`. The helper below is specific to that convention.
It checks exact IDs, coordinates, and allele pairs against both genotype files,
removes palindromic SNPs and duplicate positions, and aligns effects to reference
allele1. It does not infer strand flips or genome builds. A new dataset requires
its own harmonization workflow.

Both methods start with this **unclumped** common pool. C+T then selects a
subset; LDpred2 uses joint LD information to shrink effects across the pool.
Clumping after restricting to target variants avoids choosing a lead SNP that
cannot be scored and then losing its available correlated alternatives.

```{r harmonization-helper, echo=FALSE}
# Harmonize the supplied workshop files, whose IDs have four colon-separated
# fields: chromosome or rsID, position, allele, allele. No strand flips are used.
prepare_candidates <- function(ss, ref_bim, target_bim) {
  if (!requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Install data.table before preparing variants.")
  }
  ss <- data.table::as.data.table(data.table::copy(ss))
  ref_bim <- data.table::as.data.table(data.table::copy(ref_bim))
  target_bim <- data.table::as.data.table(data.table::copy(target_bim))
  ss_columns <- c("CHR", "SNP", "BP", "A1", "TEST", "NMISS", "BETA", "STAT", "P")
  bim_columns <- c("CHR", "SNP", "CM", "BP", "allele1", "allele2")
  for (item in list(list(ss, ss_columns, "Summary statistics"),
                    list(ref_bim, bim_columns, "Reference BIM"),
                    list(target_bim, bim_columns, "Target BIM"))) {
    missing <- setdiff(item[[2]], names(item[[1]]))
    if (length(missing)) {
      stop(item[[3]], " missing columns: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
    }
    if (anyDuplicated(as.character(item[[1]]$SNP))) {
      stop(item[[3]], " contains duplicate SNP IDs.")
    }
  }
  as_number <- function(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x)))
  chr_label <- function(x) sub("^chr", "", as.character(x), ignore.case = TRUE)
  ss[, SNP := as.character(SNP)]
  ref_bim[, SNP := as.character(SNP)]
  target_bim[, SNP := as.character(SNP)]

  audit <- data.table::data.table(stage = character(), reason = character(),
                                  before = integer(), removed = integer(),
                                  retained = integer())
  dat <- ss
  keep_rows <- function(keep, stage, reason) {
    keep[is.na(keep)] <- FALSE
    n_before <- nrow(dat)
    dat <<- dat[keep]
    audit <<- data.table::rbindlist(list(audit, data.table::data.table(
      stage = stage, reason = reason, before = n_before,
      removed = n_before - nrow(dat), retained = nrow(dat))))
    if (!nrow(dat)) stop("No eligible variants remain after ", stage, ": ", reason)
  }
  keep_rows(!is.na(dat$SNP) & nzchar(dat$SNP) & dat$TEST == "ADD",
            "additive_tests", "Retain nonempty SNP IDs with TEST = ADD.")
  keep_rows(dat$SNP %in% ref_bim$SNP & dat$SNP %in% target_bim$SNP,
            "shared_ids", "Require an exact SNP ID in both genotype datasets.")

  dat[, reference_row := match(SNP, ref_bim$SNP)]
  dat[, target_row := match(SNP, target_bim$SNP)]
  dat[, CHR := chr_label(CHR)]
  dat[, BP := as_number(BP)]
  ref_chr <- chr_label(ref_bim$CHR[dat$reference_row])
  target_chr <- chr_label(target_bim$CHR[dat$target_row])
  ref_bp <- as_number(ref_bim$BP[dat$reference_row])
  target_bp <- as_number(target_bim$BP[dat$target_row])
  keep_rows(!is.na(dat$CHR) & nzchar(dat$CHR) & is.finite(dat$BP) &
              dat$BP > 0 & dat$BP == floor(dat$BP) &
              dat$CHR == ref_chr & dat$CHR == target_chr &
              dat$BP == ref_bp & dat$BP == target_bp,
            "matching_coordinates", "Require matching chromosome and base-pair position.")

  # Only the supplied four-field ID convention is accepted. An rsID first
  # field has no embedded chromosome; numeric chromosome fields are checked.
  tokens <- strsplit(dat$SNP, ":", fixed = TRUE)
  valid_length <- lengths(tokens) == 4L
  fields <- matrix(NA_character_, nrow(dat), 4L)
  if (any(valid_length)) fields[valid_length, ] <- do.call(rbind, tokens[valid_length])
  embedded_chr <- grepl("^(chr)?[0-9]+$", fields[, 1], ignore.case = TRUE)
  valid_first <- embedded_chr | grepl("^rs[0-9]+$", fields[, 1])
  dat[, id_allele1 := fields[, 3]]
  dat[, id_allele2 := fields[, 4]]
  keep_rows(valid_length & valid_first &
              as_number(fields[, 2]) == dat$BP &
              (!embedded_chr | chr_label(fields[, 1]) == dat$CHR),
            "composite_ids", "Require the supplied four-field ID and matching embedded coordinates.")

  dat[, ref_a1 := as.character(ref_bim$allele1[reference_row])]
  dat[, ref_a2 := as.character(ref_bim$allele2[reference_row])]
  dat[, target_a1 := as.character(target_bim$allele1[target_row])]
  dat[, target_a2 := as.character(target_bim$allele2[target_row])]
  bases <- c("A", "C", "G", "T")
  keep_rows(dat$id_allele1 %in% bases & dat$id_allele2 %in% bases &
              dat$id_allele1 != dat$id_allele2 &
              dat$ref_a1 %in% bases & dat$ref_a2 %in% bases &
              dat$ref_a1 != dat$ref_a2 &
              dat$target_a1 %in% bases & dat$target_a2 %in% bases &
              dat$target_a1 != dat$target_a2,
            "biallelic_snps", "Require two distinct single-base A/C/G/T alleles.")
  allele_key <- function(a, b) paste0(pmin(a, b), pmax(a, b))
  id_key <- allele_key(dat$id_allele1, dat$id_allele2)
  keep_rows(!id_key %in% c("AT", "CG"),
            "unambiguous_alleles", "Remove palindromic A/T and C/G SNPs.")
  id_key <- allele_key(dat$id_allele1, dat$id_allele2)
  keep_rows(allele_key(dat$ref_a1, dat$ref_a2) == id_key &
              allele_key(dat$target_a1, dat$target_a2) == id_key &
              (dat$A1 == dat$id_allele1 | dat$A1 == dat$id_allele2),
            "matching_alleles", "Require both genotype allele pairs and the GWAS effect allele to agree with the ID.")

  locus <- paste(dat$CHR, dat$BP, sep = ":")
  keep_rows(!duplicated(locus) & !duplicated(locus, fromLast = TRUE),
            "unique_positions", "Remove every candidate at a duplicated chromosome-position pair.")
  for (column in c("NMISS", "BETA", "STAT", "P")) {
    data.table::set(dat, j = column, value = as_number(dat[[column]]))
  }
  dat[, SE := BETA / STAT]
  keep_rows(is.finite(dat$BETA) & is.finite(dat$STAT) & dat$STAT != 0 &
              is.finite(dat$SE) & dat$SE > 0 &
              is.finite(dat$NMISS) & dat$NMISS > 2 &
              dat$NMISS == floor(dat$NMISS) &
              is.finite(dat$P) & dat$P >= 0 & dat$P <= 1,
            "valid_statistics", "Require a positive signed BETA/STAT standard error, integer NMISS > 2, and valid P.")

  dat[, GWAS_A1 := as.character(A1)]
  dat[, beta_reversed := GWAS_A1 != ref_a1]
  dat[, BETA := ifelse(beta_reversed, -BETA, BETA)]
  dat[, `:=`(A1 = ref_a1, A2 = ref_a2)]
  data.table::setorder(dat, reference_row)
  manifest <- dat[, .(SNP, CHR, BP, A1, A2, BETA, SE, NMISS, P,
                       GWAS_A1, beta_reversed)]
  list(manifest = manifest, audit = audit)
}
```

```{r common-variants}
read_bim <- function(prefix) {
  x <- fread(paste0(prefix, ".bim"), header = FALSE, colClasses = "character")
  setnames(x, c("CHR", "SNP", "CM", "BP", "allele1", "allele2"))
  x
}
# Subset the large reference with PLINK before reading its BIM into R.
# This avoids importing variants that cannot enter either score.
target_bim <- read_bim(geno_file)
initial_ids <- intersect(EUR_sum$SNP, target_bim$SNP)
if (!length(initial_ids)) stop("No shared summary and target SNP IDs.")
initial_file <- file.path(run_dir, "initial_shared_ids.txt")
writeLines(initial_ids, initial_file)
initial_ref <- file.path(run_dir, "initial_reference")
run_plink("1", c("--bfile", ref_data, "--extract", initial_file,
                 "--keep-allele-order", "--make-bed", resource_args,
                 "--out", initial_ref), "initial_reference_subset")
ref_bim <- read_bim(initial_ref)
prepared <- prepare_candidates(EUR_sum, ref_bim, target_bim)
manifest <- prepared$manifest
if (any(manifest$CHR != "22")) stop("This exercise expects chromosome 22 only.")
if (!is.finite(params$ref_maf) || params$ref_maf <= 0 || params$ref_maf >= .5 ||
    !is.finite(params$ref_geno) || params$ref_geno < 0 || params$ref_geno > 1) {
  stop("Invalid reference QC parameters.")
}
candidate_file <- file.path(run_dir, "candidate_snps.txt")
writeLines(manifest$SNP, candidate_file)
common_ref <- file.path(run_dir, "common_reference")
run_plink("1", c("--bfile", initial_ref, "--extract", candidate_file,
                 "--maf", params$ref_maf, "--geno", params$ref_geno,
                 "--keep-allele-order", "--make-bed", resource_args,
                 "--out", common_ref), "reference_qc")
common_bim <- read_bim(common_ref)
if (!nrow(common_bim) || !all(common_bim$SNP %in% manifest$SNP)) {
  stop("Unexpected reference subset.")
}
n_before_qc <- nrow(manifest)
manifest <- manifest[match(common_bim$SNP, manifest$SNP)]
stopifnot(identical(manifest$A1, common_bim$allele1),
          identical(manifest$A2, common_bim$allele2),
          all(diff(manifest$BP) > 0))
audit <- rbind(prepared$audit, data.table(stage = "reference_qc",
  reason = "Reference MAF and genotype missingness filters.",
  before = n_before_qc, removed = n_before_qc - nrow(manifest),
  retained = nrow(manifest)))
fwrite(audit, file.path(run_dir, "variant_audit.tsv"), sep = "\t")
fwrite(manifest, file.path(run_dir, "variant_manifest.tsv"), sep = "\t")
common_sum_file <- file.path(run_dir, "common_summary.tsv")
fwrite(manifest, common_sum_file, sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(audit[, .(stage, before, removed, retained)])
cat("Eligible variants:", nrow(manifest),
    "\nReference individuals:", nrow(fread(paste0(common_ref, ".fam"))),
    "\nEffects reversed to reference allele1:", sum(manifest$beta_reversed), "\n")
```

The reference MAF filter removes monomorphic and very rare reference variants;
the genotype missingness filter limits missing calls. The LD matrix below uses
pairwise complete reference genotypes. These choices are fixed before tuning.

# LD clumping with PLINK 1.9

Clumping selects a lead SNP and groups nearby SNPs correlated with it, starting
with the smallest GWAS p-value. We use a **500 kb radius**, **LD \(r^2 = 0.1\)**,
and `--clump-p1 1` so index SNPs across the p-value range can be considered.
LD \(r^2\) measures correlation between variants and differs from
the prediction \(R^2\) calculated later.

```{r clump}
clump_prefix <- file.path(run_dir, "LD_clump")
run_plink("1", c("--bfile", common_ref, "--clump", common_sum_file,
                 "--clump-p1", "1", "--clump-r2", params$clump_r2,
                 "--clump-kb", params$clump_kb,
                 resource_args, "--out", clump_prefix), "clumping")
clump_file <- paste0(clump_prefix, ".clumped")
if (!file.exists(clump_file)) stop("No clumps were produced; inspect the PLINK log.")
LD_clump <- fread(clump_file)
if (!"SNP" %in% names(LD_clump) || !nrow(LD_clump)) stop("No lead SNPs were found.")
clumped <- manifest[match(LD_clump$SNP, manifest$SNP), .(SNP, A1, BETA, P)]
if (anyNA(clumped)) stop("Clumped SNPs did not match the common variant pool.")
prs_prep <- copy(clumped)
cat("LD-clumped lead SNPs:", nrow(clumped), "\n")
setorder(prs_prep, P, SNP)
fwrite(prs_prep, file.path(run_dir, "clumped_score_candidates.tsv"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(head(prs_prep)[, .(SNP, A1, BETA, P = format(P, scientific = TRUE))])
```

# Calculate PRS at nine p-value thresholds

For each threshold, retain clumped SNPs with `P <= threshold` and write their
`SNP`, `A1`, and `BETA` values. `header` skips the coefficient-file header;
`1 2 3` identifies the input columns. `SCORE1_SUM` is the weighted allele sum.
With `no-mean-imputation`, a missing genotype contributes no term to the sum. Missingness can affect scores in real data.

All clumped lead SNPs come from the common eligible pool and should be scoreable.
The code verifies the actual variants used by PLINK at every threshold.

```{r score-thresholds}
pthres <- c(5e-8, 5e-7, 5e-6, 5e-5, 5e-4, 5e-3, 5e-2, 5e-1, 1)
performance <- data.table(threshold = pthres, n_lead_snps = 0L, n_scored_snps = 0L,
                           tuning_R2 = NA_real_, status = "not scored")
for (k in seq_along(pthres)) {
  prs_coeff <- prs_prep[P <= pthres[k], .(SNP, A1, BETA)]
  performance$n_lead_snps[k] <- sum(clumped$P <= pthres[k])
  performance$n_scored_snps[k] <- nrow(prs_coeff)
  if (!nrow(prs_coeff)) {
    performance$status[k] <- "no SNPs at this threshold"
    next
  }
  coefficient_file <- file.path(run_dir, paste0("prs_coeff_", k, ".tsv"))
  score_prefix <- file.path(run_dir, paste0("prs_", k))
  fwrite(prs_coeff, coefficient_file, sep = "\t")
  run_plink("2", c("--bfile", geno_file,
                   "--score", coefficient_file, "1", "2", "3", "header",
                   "no-mean-imputation", "list-variants", "cols=+fid,+scoresums,-scoreavgs",
                   resource_args, "--out", score_prefix), paste0("scoring_", k))
  used_snps <- readLines(paste0(score_prefix, ".sscore.vars"))
  if (!setequal(used_snps, prs_coeff$SNP)) stop("PLINK skipped scoring variants; inspect its log.")
  performance$status[k] <- "scored"
}
knitr::kable(performance[, .(threshold = format(threshold, scientific = TRUE),
                              n_lead_snps, n_scored_snps, status)])
```

# Select the threshold using the tuning set

Read scores by **FID and IID**, and reorder them to match the outcome table.
An empty SNP set or a constant score cannot be evaluated and is excluded from
threshold selection. Validation outcomes are not used here.

```{r tune}
read_score_file <- function(path) {
  scores <- fread(path,
                   colClasses = "character")
  setnames(scores, sub("^#", "", names(scores)))
  if (!all(c("FID", "IID", "SCORE1_SUM") %in% names(scores))) {
    stop("Missing expected columns in PLINK score output.")
  }
  key <- paste(scores$FID, scores$IID, sep = "\t")
  expected_key <- paste(samples$FID, samples$IID, sep = "\t")
  if (anyDuplicated(key) || !setequal(key, expected_key)) {
    stop("Scored sample IDs do not match the outcomes.")
  }
  score <- as.numeric(scores$SCORE1_SUM[match(expected_key, key)])
  if (any(!is.finite(score))) stop("Non-finite PRS values.")
  score
}
read_scores <- function(k) read_score_file(file.path(run_dir, paste0("prs_", k, ".sscore")))
tuning <- samples$cohort == "tuning"
if (var(samples$y[tuning]) == 0) stop("The tuning outcome is constant.")
for (k in which(performance$status == "scored")) {
  score <- read_scores(k)
  if (var(score[tuning]) == 0) {
    performance$status[k] <- "constant tuning score"
    next
  }
  model <- lm(y ~ PRS, data = data.frame(y = samples$y[tuning], PRS = score[tuning]))
  performance$tuning_R2[k] <- summary(model)$r.squared
}
eligible <- which(is.finite(performance$tuning_R2))
if (!length(eligible)) stop("No threshold produced an evaluable tuning score.")
# Thresholds are ascending; a tie selects the smaller threshold.
best_k <- eligible[which.max(performance$tuning_R2[eligible])]
fwrite(performance, file.path(run_dir, "tuning_performance.tsv"), sep = "\t")
performance_display <- copy(performance)
performance_display[, threshold := format(threshold, scientific = TRUE)]
knitr::kable(performance_display, digits = 6)
plot(performance$threshold, performance$tuning_R2, log = "x", type = "b", pch = 16,
     xlab = "GWAS p-value threshold", ylab = expression("Tuning " * R^2),
     main = "Choose the threshold using the tuning set")
points(performance$threshold[best_k], performance$tuning_R2[best_k],
       pch = 19, col = "firebrick", cex = 1.5)
```


# Compare LDpred2 using the same data

## What changes from C+T?

C+T keeps selected marginal GWAS effects after clumping. LDpred2 models
correlation between variants and estimates posterior effects under a prior
that combines zero and nonzero effects. We keep correlated SNPs in the
eligible pool and provide their LD matrix.

This exercise uses a small, prespecified grid:

| Parameter | Values | Meaning |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `p` | 0.01, 0.1 | Prior proportion of causal variants in the modeled pool |
| `h2` | 0.01, 0.1 | Candidate proportion of phenotype variance explained by the modeled pool |
| `sparse` | `FALSE` | Do not request the additional sparse solution |

These `h2` values are teaching settings, not estimates of whole-genome
heritability. A chromosome 22 subset cannot be assigned a whole-genome
heritability without justification. The grid is deliberately small for the
lab and must be fixed before examining validation outcomes. The four-model
grid omits `p = 1` because its dense Gibbs updates are slow in this example.
For an instructor extension, add `p = 1` before examining validation results
and generate a new matching prepared backup.

We use a 3,000 kb LD radius and shrink off-diagonal correlations by 0.95 to
stabilize the small reference matrix. Physical distance is used because these
files do not provide an appropriate genetic map. This is not a 3 cM window.
For research, use the method's recommended LD resources, broader parameter
search, and convergence checks. This small example does not establish that
one method predicts better in general.

## Choose prepared results or live fitting

Keep these default YAML settings to use the prepared LDpred2 results:

```yaml
execute: true
run_ldpred2: true
ldpred_mode: "prepared"
rebuild_ld: false
```

Save any YAML edits before rerunning setup or knitting. The default loads
prepared weights and scores; C+T still runs live. To fit LDpred2 yourself,
change **only** `ldpred_mode` to `"fit"` and install the fitting packages above.

For optional live fitting, the instructor supplies `06_PRS_1000G_LD.rds`, computed from the same 1000
Genomes reference and eligible variants. Students load this LD matrix and
run LDpred2; they do not calculate LD during class. Set `ld_file` to its path
if it is stored elsewhere. A missing default file is downloaded from the
GitHub release; a missing custom path or an incompatible file stops the fit.
LD is never calculated unless you explicitly set `rebuild_ld: true`.

The two supplied RDS files have different purposes:

| File | Contents | Classroom use |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `06_PRS_1000G_LD.rds` | LD matrix, ordered alleles, reference checksums, and settings | Input for optional live fitting |
| `06_PRS_LDpred2_prepared.rds` | Fitted weights and target scores, with matching metadata | Default; skips LDpred2 fitting and scoring |

A successful fit saves
`ldpred2_prepared.rds` in the run directory, including weights, scores, settings,
input checksums, and software versions. The instructor can distribute that
file as `06_PRS_LDpred2_prepared.rds`, together with this Rmd and the same
input data.

In the original instructor test, the LDpred2 section took about **6 minutes**,
the full live document about **11 minutes**, and the prepared document about
**4 minutes**. A later test on another Biowulf node was much faster; runtime
varies with the node and storage. Allow up to ten minutes for the LD loading
and fitting chunk during class.
If it is still running at that point, stop the active
chunk and wait for the Console prompt. Set `ldpred_mode: "prepared"` and
`prepared_ldpred_file` to the instructor's RDS path, then **save the Rmd**.
When running chunks, rerun `setup`, `ldpred-config`, `ldpred-fit`, and
`ldpred-score-tune`, using the C+T results already in the current session.
Then continue to validation and score comparison. In a fresh session, run
all chunks or Knit.
For a fresh prepared run, keep the default `ldpred_mode: "prepared"` and run
all chunks or Knit. If switching back from live fitting, change only that mode
and save. Keep the model grid and data settings unchanged:
the fallback checks the input files, variant order, settings, and sample IDs.
It explicitly reports that results were loaded. It does not require the LD
file, `bigsnpr`, or `bigsparser` to be installed. To run only C+T, set `run_ldpred2: false`.

```{r ldpred-config, eval=params$execute && params$run_ldpred2}
if (!params$ldpred_mode %in% c("fit", "prepared")) stop("Use fit or prepared mode.")
if (!length(params$ldpred_p) || !length(params$ldpred_h2) || any(!is.finite(params$ldpred_p)) || any(params$ldpred_p <= 0 | params$ldpred_p > 1) ||
    any(!is.finite(params$ldpred_h2)) || any(params$ldpred_h2 <= 0 | params$ldpred_h2 > 1) ||
    !is.finite(params$ld_window_kb) || params$ld_window_kb <= 0 ||
    !is.finite(params$ld_shrink) || params$ld_shrink <= 0 || params$ld_shrink > 1 ) stop("Invalid LDpred2 settings.")
for (parameter in c("ldpred_burn_in", "ldpred_num_iter", "ldpred_seed")) {
  value <- params[[parameter]]
  if (length(value) != 1L || !is.numeric(value) || !is.finite(value) ||
      value != floor(value) || value < 1 || value > .Machine$integer.max) {
    stop(parameter, " must be a positive integer.")
  }
}
# Do not name this table params: that name belongs to R Markdown's YAML list.
ldpred_grid <- as.data.table(expand.grid(p = params$ldpred_p, h2 = params$ldpred_h2,
                                        sparse = FALSE, KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE))
ldpred_grid[, model := paste0("LD", seq_len(.N))]
ldpred_settings <- params[c("ld_window_kb", "ld_shrink", "ref_maf", "ref_geno",
                           "ldpred_p", "ldpred_h2", "ldpred_burn_in",
                           "ldpred_num_iter", "ldpred_seed")]
# Record the effective mode/settings when switching to the prepared fallback.
saveRDS(params, file.path(run_dir, "parameters_effective.rds"))
input_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(inputs))
names(input_md5) <- c("summary", "ref_bed", "ref_bim", "ref_fam",
                     "target_bed", "target_bim", "target_fam", "outcomes")
knitr::kable(ldpred_grid)
cat("LDpred2 mode:", params$ldpred_mode, "\n")
```

## Load the supplied LD matrix and estimate joint weights

For the live exercise, inspect the four-row grid, run the fit, and then run
the scoring and tuning chunk. Record the selected `p` and `h2` before opening
the validation results. The preparation helper is supplied code; students
do not need to rewrite it during the lab.

The rows and columns of the LD matrix, summary-statistic rows, and genotype
columns must have exactly the same order and allele coding. `bigsnpr` counts
reference allele1; our manifest is aligned to that allele. The assertions
below are part of the analysis, not optional checks.

The supplied matrix already includes the stated 0.95 shrinkage. The loader
checks this flag and the settings and does not apply shrinkage again.
The optional instructor appendix shows how to rebuild this file before class.

```{r ld-builder, include=FALSE, eval=params$execute && params$run_ldpred2}
choose_ld_tempdir <- function(job_id = Sys.getenv("SLURM_JOB_ID"),
                             scratch_root = "/lscratch") {
  if (length(job_id) == 1L && !is.na(job_id) && grepl("^[0-9]+$", job_id)) {
    scratch <- file.path(scratch_root, job_id)
    if (dir.exists(scratch) && file.access(scratch, 2L) == 0L) {
      probe <- tempfile("PRS_LD_write_test_", tmpdir = scratch)
      if (isTRUE(suppressWarnings(file.create(probe)))) {
        unlink(probe)
        return(normalizePath(scratch))
      }
    }
  }
  tempdir()
}

validate_ld_bundle <- function(bundle, manifest, params, input_md5) {
  expected_variants <- as.data.frame(manifest[, .(CHR, SNP, BP, A1, A2)])
  expected_settings <- params[c("ld_window_kb", "ld_shrink", "ref_maf", "ref_geno")]
  expected_reference <- input_md5[c("ref_bed", "ref_bim", "ref_fam")]
  if (!is.list(bundle) || !identical(bundle$schema, 1L) ||
      !identical(bundle$variants, expected_variants) ||
      !identical(bundle$reference_md5, expected_reference) ||
      !identical(bundle$settings, expected_settings) ||
      !identical(bundle$shrinkage_applied, TRUE)) {
    stop("The LD file does not match the reference, variants, alleles, or LD settings.")
  }
  if (!is.character(bundle$versions) ||
      !all(c("bigsnpr", "bigsparser", "Matrix") %in% names(bundle$versions)) ||
      anyNA(bundle$versions) || any(!nzchar(bundle$versions)) ||
      !is.character(bundle$created) || length(bundle$created) != 1L ||
      is.na(bundle$created) || !nzchar(bundle$created)) {
    stop("The LD file is missing software-version or creation metadata.")
  }
  x <- bundle$corr
  if (!inherits(x, "dsCMatrix") || !identical(x@uplo, "U") ||
      !isTRUE(methods::validObject(x, test = TRUE)) ||
      !identical(dim(x), c(nrow(manifest), nrow(manifest)))) {
    stop("The LD file must contain a valid upper-triangle symmetric sparse matrix of the expected size.")
  }
  if (any(!is.finite(x@x)) || any(abs(x@x) > 1 + 1e-8) ||
      any(abs(Matrix::diag(x) - 1) > 1e-8)) {
    stop("The LD file contains invalid correlations or a non-unit diagonal.")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

shrink_ld_offdiagonal <- function(corr_sparse, shrink) {
  if (!inherits(corr_sparse, "dsCMatrix") || !identical(corr_sparse@uplo, "U") ||
      length(shrink) != 1L || !is.numeric(shrink) || !is.finite(shrink) ||
      shrink <= 0 || shrink > 1) stop("Invalid LD matrix or shrinkage factor.")
  # In a valid upper-triangle CSC matrix, a stored diagonal is the final
  # entry in its column. Check that every column has that unit diagonal.
  diagonal_positions <- corr_sparse@p[-1L]
  if (any(diff(corr_sparse@p) < 1L) ||
      !identical(corr_sparse@i[diagonal_positions], seq_len(ncol(corr_sparse)) - 1L) ||
      any(!is.finite(corr_sparse@x[diagonal_positions])) ||
      any(abs(corr_sparse@x[diagonal_positions] - 1) > 1e-8)) {
    stop("Expected a stored unit diagonal in every LD column.")
  }
  # Equivalent to shrink * R + (1 - shrink) * I without sparse addition.
  corr_sparse@x <- shrink * corr_sparse@x
  corr_sparse@x[diagonal_positions] <- 1
  corr_sparse@factors <- list()
  corr_sparse
}

build_ld_bundle <- function(common_ref, manifest, params, input_md5, threads, run_dir) {
  genotype_rds <- bigsnpr::snp_readBed(paste0(common_ref, ".bed"),
                                     backingfile = tempfile("reference_matrix_", tmpdir = run_dir))
  reference <- bigsnpr::snp_attach(genotype_rds)
  G <- reference$genotypes
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(reference$map$marker.ID), manifest$SNP),
            identical(as.character(reference$map$allele1), manifest$A1),
            identical(as.character(reference$map$allele2), manifest$A2))
  corr_sparse <- bigsnpr::snp_cor(G, size = params$ld_window_kb,
                                 infos.pos = manifest$BP, ncores = threads)
  rm(G, reference)
  invisible(gc())
  if (any(!is.finite(corr_sparse@x)) || any(abs(Matrix::diag(corr_sparse) - 1) > 1e-8)) {
    stop("Invalid LD correlations; inspect reference genotypes.")
  }
  corr_sparse <- shrink_ld_offdiagonal(corr_sparse, params$ld_shrink)
  invisible(gc())
  bundle <- list(schema = 1L, corr = corr_sparse,
    variants = as.data.frame(manifest[, .(CHR, SNP, BP, A1, A2)]),
    reference_md5 = input_md5[c("ref_bed", "ref_bim", "ref_fam")],
    settings = params[c("ld_window_kb", "ld_shrink", "ref_maf", "ref_geno")],
    shrinkage_applied = TRUE,
    versions = vapply(c("bigsnpr", "bigsparser", "Matrix"),
                      function(pkg) as.character(packageVersion(pkg)), character(1)),
    created = as.character(Sys.time()))
  validate_ld_bundle(bundle, manifest, params, input_md5)
  bundle
}
```

```{r ldpred-fit, eval=params$execute && params$run_ldpred2}
ldpred_timing <- data.table(step = character(), seconds = numeric())
if (params$ldpred_mode == "prepared") {
  backup_file <- path.expand(params$prepared_ldpred_file)
  if (!nzchar(backup_file) || !file.exists(backup_file)) stop("Provide the prepared RDS file.")
  backup <- readRDS(backup_file)
  if (!identical(backup$schema, 1L) || !identical(backup$input_md5, input_md5) ||
      !identical(backup$settings, ldpred_settings) ||
      !identical(backup$manifest, as.data.frame(manifest)) ||
      !identical(backup$grid, as.data.frame(ldpred_grid))) {
    stop("Prepared results do not match these inputs, variants, or settings.")
  }
  ldpred_weights <- backup$weights
  fit_status <- backup$fit_status
  fit_versions <- backup$versions
  ldpred_timing <- as.data.table(backup$timing)
  cat("Loaded prepared LDpred2 weights and scores from:", backup_file, "\n")
} else {
  needed <- c("bigsnpr", "bigsparser", "Matrix")
  missing <- needed[!vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
  if (length(missing)) stop("Install before class: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
                            "; or switch to prepared mode.")
  if (!is.character(params$ld_file) || length(params$ld_file) != 1L ||
      is.na(params$ld_file) || !nzchar(params$ld_file)) stop("Set ld_file to the supplied LD RDS path.")
  ld_path <- path.expand(params$ld_file)
  if (isTRUE(params$rebuild_ld)) {
    build_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
    ld_bundle <- build_ld_bundle(common_ref, manifest, params, input_md5, threads, run_dir)
    saveRDS(ld_bundle, ld_path)
    ldpred_timing <- rbind(ldpred_timing, data.table(step = "Build LD (instructor only)",
      seconds = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - build_start))
    cat("Saved instructor LD matrix:", ld_path, "\n")
  }
  if (!file.exists(ld_path) && identical(params$ld_file, "06_PRS_1000G_LD.rds")) {
    # Download the supplied matrix once; keep incomplete downloads out of the cache.
    (function() {
      old_options <- options(timeout = max(600, getOption("timeout")))
      on.exit(options(old_options), add = TRUE)
      download_path <- tempfile("LD_download_", tmpdir = dirname(ld_path), fileext = ".rds")
      on.exit(unlink(download_path), add = TRUE)
      cat("Downloading supplied LD matrix from GitHub...\n")
      download.file(
        "https://github.com/DCEG-workshops/statgen_workshop_tutorial/releases/download/prs-tutorial-2026-10-27/06_PRS_1000G_LD.rds",
        destfile = download_path, mode = "wb")
      expected_sha256 <- "49705b768abc564e361f64f4de5384b9d90a64ec11d65a2fe9cacfefff78c35a"
      if (!identical(digest::digest(file = download_path, algo = "sha256"), expected_sha256)) {
        stop("Downloaded LD checksum mismatch; retry or use prepared mode.")
      }
      if (!file.rename(download_path, ld_path)) stop("Cannot save downloaded LD file: ", ld_path)
    })()
  }
  if (!file.exists(ld_path)) {
    stop("Missing precomputed LD file: ", ld_path,
         ". Obtain it from the instructor or use prepared-score mode.")
  }
  ld_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  ld_bundle <- readRDS(ld_path)
  validate_ld_bundle(ld_bundle, manifest, params, input_md5)
  corr_sparse <- ld_bundle$corr  # Already shrunk; do not shrink a second time.
  ld_tmpdir <- choose_ld_tempdir()
  corr <- bigsparser::as_SFBM(corr_sparse,
                            backingfile = tempfile("LD_matrix_", tmpdir = ld_tmpdir), compact = TRUE)
  cat("Temporary LD backing file:", corr$sbk, "\n")
  ldpred_timing <- rbind(ldpred_timing, data.table(step = "Load LD and create SFBM",
                                                 seconds = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - ld_start))
  cat("Loaded precomputed LD for", nrow(corr_sparse), "variants from:", ld_path,
      "\nLD created:", ld_bundle$created, "\n")
  df_beta <- data.frame(beta = manifest$BETA, beta_se = manifest$SE,
                        n_eff = manifest$NMISS)
  fit_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  set.seed(params$ldpred_seed)
  ldpred_weights <- bigsnpr::snp_ldpred2_grid(
    corr, df_beta, grid_param = as.data.frame(ldpred_grid[, .(p, h2, sparse)]),
    burn_in = params$ldpred_burn_in, num_iter = params$ldpred_num_iter,
    ncores = threads)
  ldpred_timing <- rbind(ldpred_timing, data.table(step = "LDpred2 fitting",
                                                 seconds = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - fit_start))
  ldpred_weights <- as.matrix(ldpred_weights)
  fit_status <- ifelse(colSums(!is.finite(ldpred_weights)) == 0, "finite weights", "nonfinite weights")
  fit_versions <- vapply(needed, function(pkg) as.character(packageVersion(pkg)), character(1))
}
stopifnot(identical(dim(ldpred_weights), c(nrow(manifest), nrow(ldpred_grid))))
fit_status <- ifelse(colSums(!is.finite(ldpred_weights)) == 0, "finite weights", "nonfinite weights")
if (!any(fit_status == "finite weights")) stop("All LDpred2 fits failed.")
colnames(ldpred_weights) <- ldpred_grid$model
rownames(ldpred_weights) <- manifest$SNP
knitr::kable(cbind(ldpred_grid, fit_status))
```

Nonfinite coefficients indicate a failed model and exclude it from tuning.
Finite coefficients alone do not establish MCMC convergence. The short run is
for teaching; a research analysis needs longer runs and stability assessment.
In the supplied instructor backup, both `h2 = 0.1` candidates have nonfinite
weights and are excluded. The two `h2 = 0.01` candidates can be scored.
Inspect these statuses before selecting a model; an excluded candidate has
zero scored SNPs and no tuning R-squared.

## Score the target samples and tune LDpred2

The score formula stays the same. We replace the marginal GWAS coefficients
with LDpred2 posterior coefficients. PLINK uses the specified effect allele
even when the target BIM lists its alleles in the opposite order. Both methods
use `SCORE1_SUM` and the same missing-genotype policy.

```{r ldpred-score-tune, eval=params$execute && params$run_ldpred2}
score_start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
ldpred_scores <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(samples), nrow(ldpred_grid),
                         dimnames = list(NULL, ldpred_grid$model))
if (params$ldpred_mode == "prepared") {
  expected_key <- paste(samples$FID, samples$IID, sep = "\t")
  saved_key <- paste(backup$scores$FID, backup$scores$IID, sep = "\t")
  if (anyDuplicated(saved_key) || !setequal(saved_key, expected_key) ||
      !all(ldpred_grid$model %in% names(backup$scores))) stop("Prepared scores have incompatible IDs.")
  ldpred_scores[,] <- as.matrix(backup$scores[match(expected_key, saved_key), ldpred_grid$model, drop = FALSE])
} else {
  for (j in which(fit_status == "finite weights")) {
    weights_file <- file.path(run_dir, paste0("ldpred2_weights_", j, ".tsv"))
    score_prefix <- file.path(run_dir, paste0("ldpred2_", j))
    fwrite(data.table(SNP = manifest$SNP, A1 = manifest$A1,
                      BETA = ldpred_weights[, j]), weights_file, sep = "\t")
    run_plink("2", c("--bfile", geno_file, "--score", weights_file, "1", "2", "3", "header",
                     "no-mean-imputation", "list-variants", "cols=+fid,+scoresums,-scoreavgs",
                     resource_args, "--out", score_prefix), paste0("ldpred2_scoring_", j))
    if (!setequal(readLines(paste0(score_prefix, ".sscore.vars")), manifest$SNP)) {
      stop("PLINK skipped an LDpred2 scoring variant.")
    }
    ldpred_scores[, j] <- read_score_file(paste0(score_prefix, ".sscore"))
  }
  ldpred_timing <- rbind(ldpred_timing, data.table(step = "Target scoring",
    seconds = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - score_start))
}
ldpred_performance <- copy(ldpred_grid)
ldpred_performance[, `:=`(n_scored_snps = ifelse(fit_status == "finite weights", nrow(manifest), 0L),
                          tuning_R2 = NA_real_, status = fit_status)]
for (j in which(fit_status == "finite weights")) {
  score <- ldpred_scores[, j]
  if (any(!is.finite(score)) || var(score[tuning]) == 0) {
    ldpred_performance$status[j] <- "invalid or constant score"
    next
  }
  ldpred_performance$tuning_R2[j] <- cor(samples$y[tuning], score[tuning])^2
  ldpred_performance$status[j] <- "evaluated"
}
eligible_ld <- which(is.finite(ldpred_performance$tuning_R2))
if (!length(eligible_ld)) stop("No LDpred2 model is evaluable.")
# A tie is resolved by the first row in the prespecified grid.
best_ld <- eligible_ld[which.max(ldpred_performance$tuning_R2[eligible_ld])]
fwrite(ldpred_performance, file.path(run_dir, "ldpred2_tuning_performance.tsv"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(ldpred_performance, digits = 6)
knitr::kable(ldpred_timing, digits = 2,
              caption = if (params$ldpred_mode == "fit") "Measured live runtime" else "Runtime recorded in prepared results")
if (params$ldpred_mode == "fit") {
  backup <- list(schema = 1L, input_md5 = input_md5, settings = ldpred_settings,
                 manifest = as.data.frame(manifest), grid = as.data.frame(ldpred_grid),
                 weights = ldpred_weights, scores = data.frame(samples[, .(FID, IID)], ldpred_scores),
                 fit_status = fit_status, timing = as.data.frame(ldpred_timing),
                 versions = fit_versions, created = as.character(Sys.time()))
  saveRDS(backup, file.path(run_dir, "ldpred2_prepared.rds"))
  cat("Backup created:", file.path(run_dir, "ldpred2_prepared.rds"), "\n")
}
```

# Compare the selected scores in the validation set

Freeze one C+T threshold and one LDpred2 setting using tuning outcomes only.
Evaluate each once in the validation set. Do not expand the grid or change
QC settings after inspecting this table. Reporting both prespecified methods
is different from selecting a new model using the validation outcomes.

For one score and an intercept, the validation regression \(R^2\) equals
squared Pearson correlation. This measures association in held-out samples.
It does not test calibration of a prediction equation frozen in the tuning set.
The analysis is unadjusted because this is a simulated teaching example.

```{r validate}
validation <- samples$cohort == "validation"
best_score <- read_scores(best_k)
validation_r2 <- function(score) {
  if (any(!is.finite(score)) || var(samples$y[validation]) == 0 || var(score[validation]) == 0) {
    stop("Validation R-squared is undefined for invalid or constant data.")
  }
  cor(samples$y[validation], score[validation])^2
}
comparison <- data.table(method = "C+T", mode = "live scoring",
  selected_setting = paste0("P <= ", format(pthres[best_k], scientific = TRUE)),
  n_scored_snps = performance$n_scored_snps[best_k],
  tuning_n = sum(tuning), tuning_R2 = performance$tuning_R2[best_k],
  validation_n = sum(validation), validation_R2 = validation_r2(best_score))
selected_scores <- data.table(samples[, .(FID, IID, cohort)], CT = best_score)
if (isTRUE(params$run_ldpred2)) {
  best_ld_score <- ldpred_scores[, best_ld]
  comparison <- rbind(comparison, data.table(method = "LDpred2", mode = params$ldpred_mode,
    selected_setting = paste0("p = ", ldpred_grid$p[best_ld], "; h2 = ", ldpred_grid$h2[best_ld]),
    n_scored_snps = nrow(manifest), tuning_n = sum(tuning),
    tuning_R2 = ldpred_performance$tuning_R2[best_ld], validation_n = sum(validation),
    validation_R2 = validation_r2(best_ld_score)))
  selected_scores[, LDpred2 := best_ld_score]
}
fwrite(comparison, file.path(run_dir, "method_comparison.tsv"), sep = "\t")
fwrite(selected_scores, file.path(run_dir, "selected_scores.tsv"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 6)
barplot(rbind(comparison$tuning_R2, comparison$validation_R2), beside = TRUE,
        names.arg = comparison$method, col = c("steelblue", "darkorange"),
        ylab = expression(R^2), legend.text = c("Tuning", "Validation"),
        args.legend = list(x = "topright", bty = "n"),
        main = "Performance of the selected scores")
```

```{r score-comparison, eval=params$execute && params$run_ldpred2}
standardize_from_tuning <- function(x) (x - mean(x[tuning])) / sd(x[tuning])
plot(standardize_from_tuning(best_score)[validation],
     standardize_from_tuning(best_ld_score)[validation], pch = 16,
     col = grDevices::adjustcolor("steelblue", alpha.f = 0.15),
     xlab = "C+T PRS (tuning SD units)", ylab = "LDpred2 PRS (tuning SD units)",
     main = "Do the methods rank individuals similarly?")
cat("Correlation between validation scores:",
    round(cor(best_score[validation], best_ld_score[validation]), 4), "\n")
```

## Reproduction checks

After freezing the selected settings and running validation, compare your
results with the tested example:

| Method | Selected setting | Scored SNPs | Validation R-squared |
|:---|:---|---:|---:|
| C+T | P <= 0.0005 | 32 | 0.001808344 |
| LDpred2 | p = 0.01; h2 = 0.01 | 23,552 | 0.002521289 |

Both use 10,000 tuning samples and 10,000 separate validation samples.
These are reproduction checks, not a general method ranking. Do not change
the grid to obtain these numbers or after looking at validation results.
Report different behavior or additional errors to the instructor.

## Discussion questions

1. How does C+T's SNP count change across p-value thresholds?
2. What information does LDpred2 use that C+T discards during clumping?
3. Which `p` and `h2` combination was selected in the tuning set? Does that
   establish the true causal fraction or heritability? Explain why not.
4. Do the selected scores rank individuals similarly? Why can performance
   differ even when the same input files and sample split are used?
5. Why would selecting settings using validation outcomes give an optimistic
   performance estimate?
6. What could change with a larger LD reference, all chromosomes, covariates,
   or an ancestry-mismatched discovery or reference population?

This chromosome 22 exercise illustrates two workflows. The small European
reference and restricted variant set limit generalization. Neither result is
an estimate of clinical performance, and LDpred2 is not guaranteed to outperform
C+T in this example. PRS-CS can be discussed as another LD-aware Bayesian
method, without adding a third software workflow to this 90-minute lab.

# Optional instructor appendix: build the LD input before class

This step is outside the 90-minute lab. It calculates LD from the same
reference individuals and the complete eligible variant pool used above.
No variants are removed merely to shorten the classroom exercise.

To create or replace the LD input, set `ldpred_mode: "fit"`,
`rebuild_ld: true`, and `ld_file` to the desired output path in the YAML
header. Save the Rmd and run it from the start. The `ldpred-fit` chunk calls
the builder below, saves the portable sparse matrix and metadata, and
continues with fitting and scoring. The parent directory of `ld_file` must
already exist. Rebuilding can take substantially longer than fitting.

After a successful instructor run, restore `rebuild_ld: false` and
`ldpred_mode: "prepared"`, then save the Rmd before distributing it. Provide the saved LD file and the prepared-score
backup, renamed as shown above. Test both prepared mode and optional live
loading in a fresh session. Both files must match the supplied data and analysis settings.

The portable LD file contains matrix values and metadata, without paths to
the instructor's temporary genotype or SFBM files. Each student creates an
SFBM after loading it. On Biowulf, the code uses the job's
`/lscratch/<SLURM_JOB_ID>` directory when it exists and passes a write check.
This also works when RStudio's `tempdir()` was initialized elsewhere. Request
local scratch when launching RStudio. If no writable job scratch directory is
available, the code uses the R session's temporary directory instead. The
output prints the temporary LD file's location. These temporary files are not
part of the distributed LD input. Software versions record
how LD was calculated; they are not required to equal the student's versions.

```{r ld-builder-example, ref.label='ld-builder', eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, include=TRUE}
```

# Record the software environment

```{r session-info}
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(run_dir, "sessionInfo.txt"))
sessionInfo()
cat("Saved results:", run_dir, "\n")
```

Results are from the current run. PLINK `.log` files and `.console.log` files
contain variant counts, warnings, and versions; `.sh` files record the commands.
`parameters.rds` records the initial run configuration; `parameters_effective.rds`
records the current LDpred2 configuration, including an interactive switch to
prepared mode.

If something fails, send the instructor the **chunk name**, **exact error or
warning**, your R/package versions from `sessionInfo()`, and the relevant log
from the printed run directory. You do not need to send raw genotype files.

[PLINK 2 scoring](https://www.cog-genomics.org/plink/2.0/score), and
[Biowulf PLINK modules](https://hpc.nih.gov/apps/plink.html).
LDpred2: [official tutorial](https://privefl.github.io/bigsnpr/articles/LDpred2.html),
[function reference](https://privefl.github.io/bigsnpr/reference/LDpred2.html),
[LD calculation](https://privefl.github.io/bigsnpr/reference/snp_cor.html), and
